_meta.indication: Treatment of adults with moderately to severely active rheumatoid arthritis who have had an inadequate response or intolerance to methotrexate.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study RA-IV (also referred to as M14-465)
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, active-comparator (adalimumab) and placebo-controlled MTX add-on trial; patients randomized 2:2:1 to placebo, RINVOQ 15 mg QD, or adalimumab 40 mg every other week on background MTX. Total treatment period (TP1) of 48 weeks, with the primary analysis at Week 12.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with moderately to severely active rheumatoid arthritis who had an inadequate response to methotrexate (MTX-IR).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of patients achieving ACR20 response at Week 12.
pivotal_trials.n: N=1629 randomized (analysis N=651 placebo and 651 RINVOQ 15 mg shown for ACR20).
pivotal_trials.result: ACR20 at Week 12: 71% with RINVOQ 15 mg vs 36% with placebo (treatment difference 34%, 95% CI 29, 39).

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study RA-V (also referred to as M13-542)
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled cDMARD add-on trial; patients randomized 1:1:1 to placebo, RINVOQ 15 mg QD, or upadacitinib 30 mg QD on background cDMARDs. Total treatment period (TP1) of 24 weeks, with the primary analysis at Week 12.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with moderately to severely active rheumatoid arthritis who had an inadequate response or intolerance to biologic DMARDs (bDMARD-IR).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of patients achieving ACR20 response at Week 12.
pivotal_trials.n: N=499 randomized (analysis N=169 placebo and 164 RINVOQ 15 mg shown for ACR20).
pivotal_trials.result: ACR20 at Week 12: 65% with RINVOQ 15 mg vs 28% with placebo (treatment difference 36%, 95% CI 26, 46).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=1%) were upper respiratory tract infection (13.5% RINVOQ 15 mg vs 9.5% placebo), nausea (3.5% vs 2.2%), cough (2.2% vs 1.0%), and pyrexia (1.2% vs 0%). Serious risks include serious infections, malignancy, thrombosis, gastrointestinal perforations, and laboratory abnormalities.
target_moa: Upadacitinib is an oral, selective Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor (selective JAK-1 inhibitor) that modulates the signaling pathway at the point of JAKs, preventing phosphorylation and activation of STATs and thereby modulating immune cell function.

boxed_warning.content: Boxed warning: SERIOUS INFECTIONS, MALIGNANCY, AND THROMBOSIS. Serious infections leading to hospitalization or death (including tuberculosis, bacterial, invasive fungal, viral and other opportunistic infections); lymphoma and other malignancies; and thrombosis (deep venous thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, and arterial thrombosis) have occurred.

rems.type: A Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) was determined not necessary because the risks can be adequately described in product labeling.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was held; no issues were identified warranting advisory committee input.

summary.text: RINVOQ (upadacitinib), a new molecular entity oral small-molecule JAK inhibitor, was submitted by AbbVie on December 18, 2018 and reviewed under Priority Review supported by a Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review Voucher, with a PDUFA goal date of August 18, 2019. It was approved (first cycle, no advisory committee) for moderately to severely active RA in MTX inadequate responders; no REMS was required and pediatric studies were required under PREA.

citations.quote: AbbVie submitted new drug application (NDA) 211675 on December 18, 2018, for the new molecular entity (NME) upadacitinib, an oral small molecule inhibitor of the Janus associated kinases (JAK)
The Applicant requested a Priority Review and used Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review Voucher No. PRV BLA 125516 to support their request.

Given that the safety profile of upadacitinib is generally consistent with other immunosuppressants and JAK inhibitors approved for RA patients, the risks can be adequately described in product labeling and a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) is not necessary.
An advisory committee meeting was not held for this application. No issues were identified warranting advisory committee input.
